subject: Physics
basis: NCERT Physics section -> Maharashtra State Board section, the edge the /dashboard/syllabus alignment table's NCERT column and the chapter matrix's CBSE column both read. Authored 2026-08-05 by five agents against scripts/syllabus/RULING_BRIEF.md, each verdict decided by searching the actual book TEXT per chapter (generated-papers/physics-corpus.json via search_corpus.py), never by matching a section title. Before this the edge had ZERO rows for Physics and the page rendered 'not in NCERT' on all 318 alignment rows - a checked-claim label over an unchecked blank, false for e.g. Dimensional Analysis. Reviewer spot-verified every falsifiable zero-hit claim; counts quoted in the notes were re-run and matched.

stateBoard.note: XI:1.9 defines significant figures from least count and gives the determination plus arithmetic/rounding rules ('significant figures' 11 hits, all in XI ch.1). It sits at the END of the State Board chapter, after the error sections NCERT dropped, rather than at 1.3.

The State Board does not split formulae/equations into their own section; 'dimensional formula' scores 9 hits in XI ch.1, all inside XI:1.6, which writes the dimensional formula and equation for each quantity.

XI:1.6.1 gives the same three applications NCERT does — checking correctness by homogeneity (worked on v = u + at), establishing a relation (the simple pendulum) and unit conversion — and XI:1.6.2 adds the limitations.

The State Board has NO 'Motion in a Straight Line' chapter. One-dimensional motion is XI:3.2 Rectilinear Motion, inside the Motion in a Plane chapter, which opens with displacement vs path length and average velocity vs average speed.

XI:3.2 defines instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocity (v = dx/dt) and reads it off the tangent to the x-t graph; XI:3.3.1 repeats it for the plane. 13 of the 14 State Board 'instantaneous velocity' hits are in XI ch.3.
Average and instantaneous acceleration, the v-t graph slope and the area-under-v-t result are all inside XI:3.2; XI:3.3.2 restates them vectorially for the plane.

rulings.subtopic: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

stateBoard.note: XI:3.2 derives all three equations graphically from the v-t graph (eqs 3.7-3.9) and applies them to free fall; XI:3.3.3 gives the vector form for a plane.
Vectors are taught in the State Board's own MATHEMATICAL METHODS chapter (XI ch.2), which NCERT has no counterpart for, not inside the kinematics chapter.

rulings.subtopic: Multiplication of Vectors by Real Numbers
Addition and Subtraction of Vectors - Graphical Method

stateBoard.note: XI:2.4 resolves a vector into rectangular components with unit vectors in two and three dimensions, and recovers magnitude and direction from the components (eqs 2.12-2.15).

XI:2.3.4 derives the parallelogram-law resultant and direction angle; XI:2.4 gives component/unit-vector addition. The State Board has no separately titled 'analytical method' heading — the content is split across these two.
XI:3.3.4 additionally teaches relative velocity (12 hits in XI ch.3), which the rationalised NCERT section no longer carries.

rulings.subtopic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration

stateBoard.note: XI:3.4.1 gives period, radius vector and angular speed; XI:3.4.2 derives the centripetal acceleration. The State Board then re-teaches circular motion far more deeply in Std XII ch.1 Rotational Dynamics.

Same title and same content: Aristotle's claim that an external force is needed to keep a body in uniform motion, and Galileo's correction that friction and viscous drag are what stop things ('Aristotle' 5 hits in XI ch.4).

The PHRASE 'law of inertia' is ZERO in the State Board — it is NCERT's name, not this book's. The content is there: XI:4.3 states the first law and XI:4.3.1 defines inertia as the property by which an object resists a change in its state of motion, measured as inertial mass ('inertia' 20 hits in XI ch.4).
The State Board states all three laws together in XI:4.3 and then devotes 4.3.1-4.3.3 to the importance of each, rather than giving each law its own numbered section.
XI:4.3.2 insists on F = dp/dt as primary and derives F = ma only for constant mass (using the rocket as the counter-example). Impulse, which NCERT folds into this section, is XI:4.9.
XI:4.7 derives it from F = dp/dt and states it for an isolated system, distinguishing internal from external forces during collision and explosion.
XI:4.12 Mechanical equilibrium gives the same condition; XI:4.12.1 adds stable/unstable/neutral equilibrium via potential energy, which NCERT's section does not carry.

Friction is NOT in the Laws of Motion chapter — it is XI:6.9 in Mechanical Properties of Solids, with static/kinetic/rolling friction and both coefficients. 'coefficient of friction' returns ZERO because the book only ever writes 'coefficient of static friction' / 'coefficient of kinetic friction'. The spring force appears later, at XII:5.3.

Cross-year: the dynamics NCERT puts in Laws of Motion is Std XII here. XII:1.2.2 gives centripetal/centrifugal force, XII:1.3.1 the level track and XII:1.3.3 the banked road ('banked' 15 hits, all in XII ch.1). The State Board also adds the well of death, conical pendulum and vertical circular motion.

'free body' scores 15 hits in XI ch.4, in an UNNUMBERED subsection on systems and free body diagrams inside XI:4.7 — hence the cite. It works a multi-pulley system and draws an FBD per mass, which is NCERT's method.

The State Board has NO Work, Energy and Power chapter — the material is folded into XI ch.4 Laws of Motion. The scalar product NCERT introduces here is XI:2.5.1, which derives W = F.s cos(theta) as its physical example.

rulings.subtopic: Notions of Work and Kinetic Energy: the Work-energy Theorem

stateBoard.note: XI:4.6 Work Energy Theorem states it, then derives it from v^2 - u^2 = 2as multiplied through by m/2.

W = Fs cos(theta) is derived in XI:2.5.1 as the physical meaning of the dot product and restated in XI:4.5.5 with its constant-force restriction. There is no numbered 'Work' section and no systematic positive/zero/negative-work discussion — 'negative work' occurs only in XII ch.4 Thermodynamics.

No standalone kinetic-energy section: the chapter's 'Can you recall?' treats KE as known from earlier classes, and 1/2 mv^2 is introduced inside XI:4.6 then used throughout collisions and rotation. 'kinetic energy' scores 26 hits in XI ch.4.

rulings.subtopic: Work Done by a Variable Force

stateBoard.note: Same title. XI:4.5.5 builds the integral from infinitesimal displacements, gives W as the area under the F-s curve, and works a numerical example.

rulings.subtopic: The Work-energy Theorem for a Variable Force

stateBoard.note: XI:4.6 Case II applies the theorem to a body falling with speed-dependent resistance, written as the integral of F ds and referring back to XI:4.5.5. The State Board reaches the same integral form without NCERT's separate dK/dt = Fv derivation.

XI:4.5.4 is titled '...and Concept of Potential Energy' and gives dW = F dx = -dU, path-independence of conservative forces and the resulting definition; XI:5.7 develops gravitational PE in detail, as 4.5.4 itself promises.

The principle is STATED inside XI:4.5.4 rather than in a section of its own, and 'conservation of mechanical energy' as a phrase is ZERO. It is applied quantitatively in XII:1.4 vertical circular motion, XII:5.11 SHM energy and XI:5.7.2.

rulings.subtopic: The Potential Energy of a Spring

stateBoard.note: Cross-year, and not in the mechanics chapter: 'spring' has exactly ONE hit in XI ch.4 and it is an exercise. XII:5.11 does NCERT's derivation exactly — integrating F = -kx to PE = 1/2 kx^2 with total energy 1/2 kA^2. XI:6.7 Strain Energy independently derives the same for a stretched wire.

No section teaches power. P = dW/dt = F.v appears only in the translational-rotational analogy table at the end of XII ch.1 and one worked example there; in XI ch.4 the definition appears only INSIDE an exercise. MISSING: any definition of average vs instantaneous power, and the practical units — 'kilowatt' and 'horsepower' are both ZERO across the State Board. Only the watt survives, as a derived unit.

The State Board goes beyond NCERT: besides elastic/inelastic, head-on final velocities and the KE loss, it adds XI:4.8.3 the coefficient of restitution and XI:4.8.6 non-head-on collision in two dimensions.

State Board opens Rotational Dynamics (XII ch.1) by distinguishing revolution about an external point from rotation about an axis through the body. Precession, a single passing mention in NCERT 6.1, is the only element absent — 'precession' is ZERO in the State Board.

Cross-year: the State Board teaches centre of mass in Std XI ch.4 Laws of Motion, not in its Std XII Rotational Dynamics chapter. 'centre of mass' scores 59 hits there, incl. the discrete sum, the continuous integral and the negative-mass (remaining-disc) method.

XI:4.13.2 gives v_cm and XI:4.13.3 a_cm, both discrete and continuous. NCERT's M*A = F_ext is stated in XI:4.13.4 as characteristics rather than as a derived equation: only an external unbalanced force moves the CoM, internal forces never do.

rulings.subtopic: Linear Momentum of a System of Particles

stateBoard.note: XI:4.7 states F = dp/dt for a system, defines an isolated system, and works the internal-vs-external force distinction for collisions and explosions before concluding momentum conservation.
Taught in the State Board's Std XI ch.2 Mathematical Methods, a chapter NCERT has no counterpart for; NCERT instead introduces the cross product inside ch.6 itself.

rulings.subtopic: Angular Velocity and Its Relation with Linear Velocity

stateBoard.note: XII:1.2.1 states v = omega x r with the right-hand thumb rule for the direction of omega; XI:3.4.1 introduces angular speed and the radius vector in Std XI.
Cross-year: torque as the rotational analogue of force and the couple are Std XI (4.10, 4.11); angular momentum L = r x p, L = I*omega and tau = dL/dt are Std XII (1.8, 1.8.1 and the analogy table).

MISSING the rotational-equilibrium condition: XI:4.12 defines mechanical equilibrium by net force = 0 only, and 'rotational equilibrium' / 'translational equilibrium' are ZERO across the whole State Board corpus. Also absent are the principle of moments, levers and mechanical advantage — 'principle of moments', 'lever', 'fulcrum' and 'mechanical advantage' all return ZERO. Taught: couple and its torque, stable/unstable/neutral equilibrium, centre of gravity.

XII:1.5 derives I from rotational KE, 1.5.1/1.5.2 do the ring and the disc, 1.6 the radius of gyration and 1.7 both the parallel- and perpendicular-axes theorems; the chapter closes with a standard-bodies MI table.

rulings.subtopic: Kinematics of Rotational Motion About a Fixed Axis

stateBoard.note: XII:1.2.1 defines angular displacement, velocity and acceleration as the analogues of s, v and a, and states that for constant axial alpha the rotational kinematical equations are those of Table 1.1.

rulings.subtopic: Dynamics of Rotational Motion About a Fixed Axis

stateBoard.note: XII:1.9 derives tau = I*alpha from the tangential forces on the constituent particles; rotational KE is in XII:1.5; the analogy table gives W = tau*theta and P = tau*omega, and XII:1.11 applies the set to rolling down an incline.

rulings.subtopic: Angular Momentum in Case of Rotation About a Fixed Axis

stateBoard.note: State Board titles it 'Measurement of the Gravitational Constant (G)'.

rulings.subtopic: Acceleration due to Gravity of the Earth
Acceleration due to Gravity Below and Above the Surface of Earth

stateBoard.note: XI:5.6 covers more than the NCERT section: variation of g with altitude, depth, latitude AND the shape of the Earth.
XI:5.7.1 derives -GMm/r, 5.7.2 reconciles it with mgh for small heights and 5.7.3 introduces gravitational potential (18 hits in that chapter).
The State Board calls it escape velocity ('escape velocity' 10 hits in XI:5 against 'escape speed' 5) and files it as a subsection of the potential-energy section rather than a section of its own.
Covers projection of a satellite, its time period, weightlessness in orbit, and both geostationary and polar satellites.
Taught as the binding energy of an orbiting satellite (10 hits in XI:5), i.e. the magnitude of the same total energy NCERT presents.
XI:6.2 Elastic Behavior of Solids carries the elasticity/plasticity, perfectly-elastic and restoring-force framing that NCERT puts in its introduction.
All four are separate subsections — Young's modulus, bulk modulus, modulus of rigidity and Poisson's ratio — and XI:6.7 adds strain energy on top.

rulings.subtopic: Applications of Elastic Behaviour of Materials

stateBoard.note: No State Board section on applications of elastic behaviour. 'girder', 'yield strength' and 'buckling' are ZERO in the State Board; 'bending' has one hit, inside XI:6.8 Hardness; the 'crane', 'pillar' and 'mountain' hits are all in unrelated chapters. NCERT's crane-rope thickness, beam-sag formula, I-section beams and maximum mountain height have no counterpart. XI:6 instead ends with strain energy, hardness and friction in solids.
Cross-year: fluids are Std XII ch.2 in the State Board and Std XI in NCERT.

Pressure due to a liquid column, atmospheric pressure, absolute vs gauge pressure, Pascal's law with the hydraulic lift/brake, and barometer/manometer measurement; XII:2.3.4 adds the hydrostatic paradox, which NCERT does not name.

XII:2.5 covers streamline vs turbulent flow, XII:2.8 the equation of continuity, and XII:2.6 critical velocity and the Reynolds number — the last absent from NCERT entirely ('Reynolds' is ZERO there).

Bernoulli's equation plus speed of efflux/Torricelli, dynamic lift on an aerofoil, the atomizer and roofs lifted by stormy wind. The one NCERT illustration absent is the spinning-ball Magnus effect ('Magnus' is ZERO in the State Board).
Viscosity and its coefficient, Stokes' law and terminal velocity are each their own subsection.

Molecular theory, surface energy, angle of contact, excess pressure across a curved surface, drops and bubbles, and capillary action (50 'capillary' hits); XII:2.4.4 adds the effect of impurity and temperature.
36 'thermometer' hits and the Celsius/Fahrenheit conversion are all in this chapter.
Linear, areal and volume expansion plus the relation between the three coefficients; the anomalous expansion of water and thermal stress are both present in XI:7 as well.
Cross-year: solids/liquids and the introduction of Cp and Cv for a gas are Std XI (7.6.1, 7.6.2); the molar specific heats and Mayer's relation are developed in Std XII ch.3 Kinetic Theory.
Sublimation, the phase diagram and triple point (13 hits), gas vs vapour, and latent heat. Regelation is the one NCERT term absent, and it is a single mention there.

Cross-year split: conduction (thermal conductivity, 21 hits), convection and radiation are Std XI ch.7; the perfect blackbody, emissivity, Stefan-Boltzmann and Wien's displacement law are Std XII ch.3, where 'blackbody' scores 56 hits against NCERT's 6.
State Board titles it 'Newton's Laws of Cooling' (plural).
Cross-year: NCERT teaches thermodynamics in Std XI, the State Board holds the whole chapter until Std XII ch.4.
'thermal equilibrium' scores 29 hits in State Board XII ch.4, plus 15 in XI:7 Thermal Properties.
'internal energy' scores 72 hits in State Board XII ch.4 against 47 in NCERT XI ch.11.

Taught in a DIFFERENT chapter, so a title scan of the State Board Thermodynamics chapter finds nothing: Cp, Cv and Cp - Cv = R are derived at XII:3.9/3.9.1 (Mayer's relation) inside Kinetic Theory of Gases, and the calorimetric definition sits at XI:7.6. XII:4.7.x then uses Cv, Cp and gamma freely.

rulings.subtopic: Thermodynamic State Variables and Equation of State

stateBoard.note: All of NCERT 11.8's named processes are present and worked: isothermal 46 hits, adiabatic 36, isobaric 15, isochoric 12, cyclic 20, quasi-static 3.
The State Board carries MORE here than NCERT: 'heat engine' 75 hits and 'refrigerator' 60 (vs 13 and 8 in NCERT), with dedicated sections on refrigerators, air conditioners and heat pumps.

No section carries this title, but the text teaches it in full: XII:4.7.3 'Classification of Thermodynamic Processes' opens with reversible and irreversible processes and gives both p-V diagrams and the friction/dissipation argument; XII:4.11.1 adds the significance of reversibility.
'Carnot' scores 33 hits in State Board XII ch.4; the book also adds a Carnot refrigerator and a Sterling cycle (XII:4.12) that NCERT does not carry.
Cross-year: NCERT teaches kinetic theory in Std XI, the State Board in Std XII ch.3 Kinetic Theory of Gases and Radiation.

Missing NCERT 12.2's historical/microscopic half: the atomic hypothesis, Dalton's atomic theory, Gay Lussac's combining volumes, Avogadro's hypothesis, molecular size and the interatomic potential-energy curve. 'atomic hypothesis', 'definite proportions', 'combining volumes' and 'interatomic potential' are all ZERO in the State Board; XII:3.4 defers Brownian motion to XI Chemistry.

Cross-year: the gas laws and PV = nRT are derived at XI:7.4.2, and XII:3.2 restates them as PV = NkT with R = N_A k plus validity conditions; XII:3.3 covers when a real gas approaches ideal. Dalton's law of partial pressures is assumed from chemistry rather than derived.

rulings.subtopic: Kinetic Theory of an Ideal Gas

stateBoard.note: XII:3.5 derives the pressure of an ideal gas from wall collisions, XII:3.6 the rms speed, XII:3.7 the kinetic interpretation of temperature — the same three results as NCERT.

Cp, Cv and Mayer's relation for monatomic, diatomic and polyatomic gases are taught in full at XII:3.9/3.9.1. MISSING is NCERT 12.6.4, the equipartition derivation of C = 3R for a SOLID: 'solid' occurs only 3 times in State Board XII ch.3, all in a recall box or numerical, and 'Dulong' is ZERO. XI:7.6.1 treats solids calorimetrically, never from equipartition.
11 hits in State Board XII ch.3, with a worked nitrogen example.
Cross-year: NCERT teaches oscillations in Std XI, the State Board in Std XII ch.5.

XII:5.3 sets up linear S.H.M. from the spring-block system, XII:5.4 gives the differential equation; phase and the graphical representation follow at 5.8/5.9. The State Board goes further than NCERT with angular S.H.M. and damped/forced oscillations.

rulings.subtopic: Simple Harmonic Motion and Uniform Circular Motion

stateBoard.note: The State Board titles it 'Reference Circle Method' — S.H.M. as the projection of uniform circular motion — so a title search for 'circular motion' in the oscillations chapter misses it.

rulings.subtopic: Velocity and Acceleration in Simple Harmonic Motion
Force Law for Simple Harmonic Motion

stateBoard.note: No section carries the NCERT title, but XII:5.3 states f = -kx with the force constant and the sign argument, and XII:5.4 turns it into the differential equation and omega = sqrt(k/m).
25 hits in State Board XII ch.5 against 15 in NCERT XI ch.13; the State Board adds the second's pendulum.
The State Board splits NCERT's Waves chapter across two years: XI ch.8 Sound carries wave basics and wave speed, XII ch.6 Superposition of Waves carries superposition, stationary waves and beats.

rulings.subtopic: Displacement Relation in a Progressive Wave

stateBoard.note: XI:8.4 writes y(x,t) = a sin(kx - wt + phi) and justifies each of a, k, omega and phi, matching NCERT 14.3.1-14.3.3; XII:6.2 restates the progressive-wave properties.

rulings.subtopic: The Speed of a Travelling Wave

stateBoard.note: Both the transverse-on-a-string and longitudinal/sound speeds are derived, and the State Board carries Newton's formula and Laplace's correction at greater length than NCERT.

rulings.subtopic: The Principle of Superposition of Waves

stateBoard.note: Stated in Std XI (XI:8.6) and then developed with pulse superposition and the resultant amplitude in Std XII ch.6.

Covers NCERT 14.6.1 Standing Waves and Normal Modes too: 'stationary wave' scores 46 hits in State Board XII ch.6 (NCERT says 'standing wave'), and XII:6.7.x gives harmonics and overtones for strings and closed/open pipes, plus end correction and the sonometer, which NCERT does not.
30 hits in State Board XII ch.6 against 11 in NCERT, with the analytical derivation of beat frequency and applications.

The State Board SPLITS electrostatics across years: XI ch.10 states charge, Coulomb's law, field, flux, Gauss's law and the dipole; XII ch.8 resumes with the applications of Gauss's law, potential and capacitance.
Includes charging by friction, contact and induction, the gold-leaf electroscope and earthing.
Cross-year: XI:10.2 introduces conductors, insulators and earthing; XII:8.7 gives the fuller treatment with free and bound charges inside a conductor.

Naming hides it from a keyword search: the State Board spells it 'Quantization of Charge' (-z-) where NCERT writes 'quantisation' (ZERO State Board hits for the -s- form), and calls additivity 'Additive Nature of Charge' — 'additivity' is ZERO while the section itself exists.
Scalar and vector forms, the unit charge definition, and relative permittivity.
Titled 'Principle of Superposition' rather than by the NCERT wording.
The State Board calls them 'Electric Lines of Force' and lists their properties with field-line figures for single, like and unlike charges.
Derives the elemental flux and the total flux integral over a closed surface.
XI:10.9.2 derives the axial and equatorial fields and concludes explicitly that the axial intensity is twice the equatorial at the same distance — NCERT's result.

rulings.subtopic: Dipole in a Uniform External Field

stateBoard.note: Titled 'Couple Acting on an Electric Dipole in a Uniform Electric Field'; gives the equal-and-opposite forces, the couple and the moment. The dipole's potential energy is added later at XII:8.6.
Defines linear, surface and volume charge densities exactly as NCERT does.
Stated and proved in Std XI, a year before NCERT teaches it.
Cross-year: the law is stated in XI:10.8 but its applications wait for Std XII ch.8 — charged spherical shell, infinitely long charged wire, and infinite charged plane sheet.
XII:8.3 defines V as work per unit charge and derives dV = -E dx, stating that the field is the negative gradient of the potential, plus the arbitrariness of the zero of potential.

rulings.subtopic: Potential due to a Point Charge
Potential due to an Electric Dipole

stateBoard.note: One State Board section, 8.4, carries NCERT's 2.3, 2.4 and 2.5 together.

rulings.subtopic: Potential due to a System of Charges

stateBoard.note: Superposition is stated in 8.4 as the algebraic sum of the individual potentials.

8.5 gives the definition, the concentric-sphere and cylindrical shapes, and zero work along the surface, i.e. E perpendicular to it. NCERT's field-potential relation is derived one section earlier, in XII:8.3.

rulings.subtopic: Potential Energy of a System of Charges

stateBoard.note: 8.6 assembles the charges from infinity, giving the two-charge result and then the general N-point-charge sum.

rulings.subtopic: Potential Energy in an External Field

stateBoard.note: All three NCERT sub-parts are present in 8.6: a single charge as qV, a two-charge system in an external field, and the dipole, derived from the external torque.
8.7 lists the same properties under electrostatic conditions — zero net field in the interior, constant potential within and on the surface — and covers electrostatic shielding.
Spelling differs: the State Board writes 'polarization' (12 hits in XII:8) where NCERT writes 'polarisation'; searching only the -s- form makes this section look thin.
XII:8.10 is titled '...Without and With Dielectric Medium Between the Plates', so it carries NCERT 2.12 and 2.13 in one section.
Series and parallel combination is folded into the same State Board section as capacitance itself.
The State Board splits current electricity across both years: XI ch.11 Electric Current Through Conductors, then XII ch.9 Current Electricity.

rulings.subtopic: Drift of Electrons and the Origin

stateBoard.note: 11.4 defines drift speed; 11.5 derives the drift velocity and resistivity relations. NAMING TRAP: 'relaxation time' is ZERO in the State Board — it calls tau 'the average time between two successive collisions'. Mobility is likewise absent here and is defined instead in XI:14.2.
11.9 derives R = rho l/A, defines conductivity, and the chapter discusses alloys and nichrome; 'manganin' is absent but the material classification is present.
'temperature coefficient of resistance' occurs 3 times in XI ch.11; superconductivity is also mentioned there.
'internal resistance' occurs 14 times in XI ch.11 and 21 times again in XII ch.9, where it is measured with the potentiometer.
NCERT's 3.11 is cells in series and in parallel; the State Board gives each its own section and adds 11.14 Types of Cells.
Std XII, not Std XI: the XI chapter stops at cells, and Kirchhoff opens the XII chapter.
XII:9.3.1 adds the metre bridge, and 9.4 the potentiometer, neither of which NCERT retains.
10.2 gives the Lorentz force; the force on a current-carrying conductor is XII:10.5, with 10.6 extending it to a closed circuit.
The State Board goes further: 10.3.1 develops the cyclotron accelerator (13 'cyclotron' hits vs 4 in NCERT), which the rationalised NCERT does not.

rulings.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Current Element, Biot-savart Law

stateBoard.note: 'Biot' occurs 12 times in XII ch.10 even though the section is titled only 'Magnetic Field due to a Current' — a case where the heading alone understates the coverage.

rulings.subtopic: Magnetic Field on the Axis of a Circular Current Loop

stateBoard.note: 10.12 additionally treats a circular arc, and 10.14 the field lines of the loop.
The State Board calls it "Ampere's Law" (13 hits in XII ch.10); the fuller phrase 'Ampere's circuital law' appears only once, so searching the NCERT name alone understates it.
XII:10.16 covers the solenoid and, unlike NCERT's rationalised section, also the toroid (11 'toroid' hits).

rulings.subtopic: Force Between Two Parallel Currents, the Ampere
Torque on Current Loop, Magnetic Dipole

stateBoard.note: 10.14 also derives the far-field axial expression and states outright that a circular current loop behaves as a magnetic dipole; 10.9 adds the dipole's magnetic potential energy.
Split across two chapters: the moving-coil instrument itself is XII:10.7.1, while its conversion to an ammeter and a voltmeter is XII:9.5.1/9.5.2 ('shunt' has 11 hits in XII ch.9).
Magnetism is a two-year split: XI ch.12 Magnetism (bar magnet, Gauss's law, earth's magnetism) and XII ch.11 Magnetic Materials.

12.2 gives the field lines, 12.3 the axial and equatorial fields, and XII:11.2 the torque on a dipole. NCERT's electrostatic analog is explicit in 12.3 as 'Table 12.1: The Electrostatic Analogue'. The one sub-part with no counterpart is 'bar magnet as an equivalent solenoid' — 'equivalent solenoid' is ZERO in the State Board.
Std XI, not XII: 12.4 states that the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero and argues it from the field lines of a bar magnet, a solenoid and an electric dipole.
SPELLING: the State Board predominantly writes 'magnetization' with a -z- (14 hits in XII ch.11 against 6 for the -s- form NCERT uses). Susceptibility and permeability are both present there.

11.5.1-11.5.3 cover dia-, para- and ferromagnetism, and 11.5.4 adds the temperature effect with the Curie point; XII:11.6-11.8 go further than NCERT with hysteresis, permanent magnets and magnetic shielding.

rulings.subtopic: The Experiments of Faraday and Henry

stateBoard.note: No separate heading, but 12.1 names Faraday's and Joseph Henry's 1831 work and describes the primary/secondary coil experiment in full — make-and-break deflection, relative motion of the coils, and rheostat-varied primary current.
Order differs: the State Board states the laws (12.2) and Lenz's law (12.3) before formalising flux in 12.4, where NCERT defines flux first.
12.2 gives both a qualitative first law and a quantitative second law.

rulings.subtopic: Lenz's Law and Conservation of Energy

stateBoard.note: 12.3.2 is titled 'Energy Conservation in Lenz's Law', and 12.9 Induction and Energy Transfer plus 12.10 Eddy Currents extend it.
Self-inductance (20 hits) and mutual inductance (26 hits) each get their own section, with worked solenoid and toroid cases; 12.12/12.13 add energy stored and energy density, which NCERT drops.

12.7 Generators derives the sinusoidal emf from Faraday's law; XII:13.2 then restates it to open the AC chapter. The phrase 'AC generator' occurs only in ch.13, so searching that term alone misses the derivation.

rulings.subtopic: AC Voltage Applied to a Resistor

stateBoard.note: XII:13.5 opens with the purely resistive AC circuit (current in phase with emf, phasor diagram); the rms/average values NCERT introduces here are defined separately in XII:13.3 'Average and RMS values' (48 'rms' hits).

rulings.subtopic: Representation of AC Current and Voltage

stateBoard.note: XII:13.4 is titled 'Phasors' and carries 26 'phasor' hits, including the rotating-vector construction and per-circuit phasor diagrams.

rulings.subtopic: AC Voltage Applied to an Inductor

stateBoard.note: Sub-block (b) of XII:13.5. Derives current lagging emf by pi/2, defines inductive reactance, notes it vanishes for DC, and Table 13.1 compares resistance with reactance. No separate heading exists, so a title search misses it.

rulings.subtopic: AC Voltage Applied to a Capacitor

stateBoard.note: Sub-block (c) of XII:13.5: current leads emf by pi/2, capacitive reactance and its phasor diagram. Again no separate heading.

rulings.subtopic: AC Voltage Applied to a Series LCR Circuit

stateBoard.note: XII:13.5 sub-block (d) gives the impedance, admittance and the phasor solution; resonance is a separate State Board section XII:13.8, with sharpness/Q factor at XII:13.9.

rulings.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit: the Power Factor

stateBoard.note: 14 'power factor' hits: cos(phi) as true power over apparent power, from the impedance triangle, plus wattless current.

NOT in the State Board AC chapter — the transformer is taught in Electromagnetic Induction as an application of mutual inductance. XII:12.15 gives the turns ratio, the ideal-transformer power relation and step-up/step-down cases. 'transformer' scores 15 hits there and ZERO in ch.13, so a title match in the AC chapter would have wrongly returned 'not'.
Cross-YEAR: EM waves are Std XI ch.13 'Electromagnetic Waves and Communication System' in the State Board. XI:13.1 covers the four laws, Maxwell's flaw in Ampere's law, Hertz, J.C. Bose and Marconi.

Split across both years. XII:8.11 'Displacement Current' (in Electrostatics) derives it for the capacitor gap; XI:13.2 states the Ampere-Maxwell law as the fourth of Maxwell's equations and XI:13.1 names displacement current as the term Maxwell added in 1861.

XI:13.2.1 'Sources of EM waves' (accelerated charges radiate); XI:13.2.2 lists transverse nature, the speed from the permittivity/permeability product, the speed in a medium, superposition and the E/B ratio.
XI:13.3 with sub-sections 13.3.1-13.3.7 matching NCERT 8.4.1-8.4.7 one for one: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.
Cross-YEAR: ray optics is Std XI ch.9 'Optics' in the State Board, not Std XII. XI:9.2 'Nature of light' and XI:9.3 'Ray optics or geometrical optics' carry the introductory material.

rulings.subtopic: Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors

stateBoard.note: XI:9.4.2 gives f = R/2, the relation between f, u and v, lateral magnification, the concave/convex image table and spherical aberration. Sign convention is XI:9.3.1. Note the book says 'mirror formula' nowhere — searching that phrase returns zero.

Snell's law, refractive index, real depth/apparent depth and the parallel-slab lateral shift. The atmospheric-refraction material is absent from BOTH books — the rationalised NCERT edition dropped it too.
Critical angle (10 hits) plus XI:9.6.1 'Applications of total internal reflection' with the optical fibre, prisms and the periscope.

XI:9.7 carries the single-surface relation, the lens makers' equation, the thin-lens formula and lenses in contact. NCERT's 'Power of a lens' is present under the State Board's own name 'Focal power' (in dioptre) — 'power of a lens' as a phrase returns zero.
XI:9.8 'Dispersion of light and prisms' — the i-delta curve, angle of minimum deviation, and the reversibility argument giving two values of i for any deviation.

XI:9.11 teaches magnifying power, the simple microscope, the compound microscope and the refracting astronomical telescope in full. MISSING: the REFLECTING telescope. NCERT devotes a figure and two paragraphs to the Cassegrain design; in the State Board 'Cassegrain', 'reflector' and 'objective mirror' are all ZERO, and the book states outright that it will discuss only the astronomical telescope.
XII:7.2 'Nature of Light' covers corpuscular, wave and dual nature, matching NCERT's historical introduction.

XII:7.4 'Huygens' Theory' with 7.4.1 primary/secondary sources, 7.4.2 wavefront (59 hits) and 7.4.3 the principle itself, including the honest caveat that the theory is empirical about backward wavelets.

rulings.subtopic: Refraction and Reflection of Plane Waves Using Huygens Principle

stateBoard.note: XII:7.5 derives i = r by the congruent-triangle wavelet construction; XII:7.6 derives Snell's law from the wave speeds and the rarer/denser bending. Both are Huygens constructions, as NCERT does them.

rulings.subtopic: Coherent and Incoherent Addition of Waves

stateBoard.note: XII:7.8.1 defines coherent sources; XII:7.8.3 gives the conditions for a well-defined steady pattern; XII:7.8 handles constructive/destructive superposition by path difference.

rulings.subtopic: Interference of Light Waves and Young's Experiment

stateBoard.note: XII:7.8.2 'Young's Double Slit Experiment' — path-difference conditions, fringe positions and fringe width, plus XII:7.8.4 on obtaining coherent sources.
XII:7.9 with 7.9.1 Fresnel vs Fraunhofer, 7.9.2 the experimental set-up, 7.9.3 Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit and 7.9.4 comparing it with the double-slit pattern. 64 'diffraction' hits.

SPELLING: the State Board writes 'polarization' with a -z- (20 hits in XII ch.7) and the -s- form NCERT uses returns ZERO in that chapter. XII:7.7 derives the Malus relation and averages over unpolarized light; XII:7.7.1 gives Brewster's law, XII:7.7.2 polarization by scattering.

The State Board has no section of this name. Work function is defined and used in depth inside XII:14.2.2 (18 hits); the three emission processes NCERT lists — thermionic, field and photo-electron emission — appear as a boxed aside near XII:14.7. Content matches, placement does not.
XII:14.2.1 gives the apparatus, XII:14.2.2 the numbered observations — photocurrent vs intensity, stopping potential (14 hits) and the threshold-frequency dependence.
XII:14.2.3 is titled 'Failure of Wave Theory to Explain the Observations from Experiments on Photoelectric Effect' — a direct counterpart.

rulings.subtopic: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation: Energy Quantum of Radiation

stateBoard.note: XII:14.2.4 'Einstein's Postulate of Quantization of Energy and the Photoelectric Equation'.

rulings.subtopic: Particle Nature of Light: the Photon

stateBoard.note: XII:14.3 'Wave-Particle Duality of Electromagnetic Radiation' carries the photon picture (68 'photon' hits); XII:14.4 adds the photo cell as an application.
XII:14.5 de Broglie hypothesis, XII:14.6 the Davisson-Germer confirmation (also G.P. Thomson), XII:14.7 wave-particle duality of matter with the scale argument and the electron microscope.
Atoms and Nuclei are TWO NCERT chapters but ONE State Board chapter, XII ch.15 'Structure of Atoms and Nuclei'; XII:15.2 covers Thomson's model.

rulings.subtopic: Alpha-particle Scattering and Rutherford's Nuclear Model of Atom

stateBoard.note: XII:15.3 'Geiger-Marsden Experiment' is the State Board's name for the alpha-scattering experiment; XII:15.4 gives the nuclear model and XII:15.4.1 its difficulties.

rulings.subtopic: Bohr Model of the Hydrogen Atom

stateBoard.note: XII:15.6.1 radii of the orbits, XII:15.6.2 energy of the electrons, XII:15.6.3 limitations of the model.

rulings.subtopic: The Line Spectra of the Hydrogen Atom

stateBoard.note: XII:15.5 names the Lyman, Balmer, Paschen, Brackett and Pfund series; XII:15.6.2 derives the wavelengths and defines Rydberg's constant.

rulings.subtopic: De Broglie's Explanation of Bohr's Second Postulate of Quantisation

stateBoard.note: XII:15.6.4 is titled 'De Broglie's Explanation' — the standing-wave justification of angular-momentum quantisation.
Nuclei has no chapter of its own in the State Board: it is the second half of XII ch.15, opening at XII:15.7 'Atomic Nucleus'.

rulings.subtopic: Atomic Masses and Composition of Nucleus

stateBoard.note: XII:15.7.1 'Constituents of a Nucleus' defines Z, N, A and the unified atomic mass unit.
XII:15.8 gives the mass defect, the binding energy and binding energy per nucleon with its curve.
XII:15.7.3 'Nuclear Forces' — the State Board pluralises the heading.
XII:15.9 treats alpha, beta and gamma decay with Q values; XII:15.10 the exponential decay law and the becquerel/curie; XII:15.10.1 half-life, XII:15.10.2 average life.
XII:15.11.1 fission with a worked Q value, the chain reaction and a controlled-fission reactor block; XII:15.11.2 fusion.
Cross-YEAR: the semiconductor material physics is Std XI ch.14 'Semiconductors' in the State Board; only the DEVICES sit in Std XII ch.16.

rulings.subtopic: Classification of Metals, Conductors and Semiconductors

stateBoard.note: XI:14.3 'Band theory of solids' builds the bands, distinguishes overlapping bands from a gap and tabulates the gap for Si, Ge and diamond. The book says 'energy gap'/'band gap' — 'forbidden' returns ZERO, so that NCERT word alone would misread as absence.
XI:14.4 covers pure Si/Ge, electron-hole pair generation and hole conduction.
XI:14.5 defines doping, n-type and p-type, donor/acceptor impurities and majority/minority carrier densities.
XI:14.6 'p-n junction' — diffusion of carriers, the depletion region (19 hits) and the potential barrier.
XI:14.7 covers forward bias (23 hits) and reverse bias (24 hits), the narrowing/widening depletion layer, both I-V characteristics and avalanche breakdown.

rulings.subtopic: Application of Junction Diode as a Rectifier

stateBoard.note: Cross-YEAR the other way: the diode is Std XI but the rectifier is Std XII ch.16 'Semiconductor Devices'. XII:16.2.1 half wave and XII:16.2.2 full wave, with 16.2.3 ripple factor and 16.2.4 filters going beyond NCERT. 'rectifier' is ZERO in the Std XI chapter, so a single-year search would wrongly return 'not'.
